notes: Read all 62 numbered source lines before editing. L1 useState/useMemo, L2 react-i18next useTranslation, L3 lucide Timer icon, L4 shared ui Input/Button/Badge, L5 ./ToolCard, L6 ./helpers describeCron/getNextCronRuns, L7 @/lib/dateFormat formatDateTime, L9-15 the CronParserTool body (expr state + parts/description/nextRuns memos), L17-23 the five presets, L25-60 the JSX (ToolCard > Input > preset Buttons > description block > next-runs list), and L62 the closing brace were each considered and reproduced natively.

Self-contained by necessity (same precedent as the sibling InfrastructureSection.tsx): the modules the source imports are NOT separate native parity targets — L5 ./ToolCard, L6 ./helpers, and the L4 shared web ui Input/Button/Badge would never resolve from native. So ToolCard, the labelled Input, the preset Buttons and the info Badge are reproduced natively in this file, and describeCron (helpers L59-75) + getNextCronRuns (helpers L77-113) are copied VERBATIM (plain TS, no DOM): the * / , - and step matchField branches, the setSeconds(0,0)+setMinutes(+1) seed, and the safety<525960 loop are byte-for-byte identical, so the computed description text and the next-run instants match the web exactly.

Behaviour/state preserved verbatim: state name expr (L11), parts = expr.trim().split(/\s+/) (L13), description = parts.length===5 ? describeCron(parts) : '' (L14), nextRuns = parts.length===5 ? getNextCronRuns(parts,5) : [] (L15), and the five preset values '* * * * *' / '0 * * * *' / '0 0 * * *' / '0 0 * * 0' / '0 0 1 * *' (L18-22). Tapping a preset calls setExpr(p.value) (L37) and the Input onChange -> onChangeText -> setExpr (L32). The description block is gated on `description` (L42) and the next-runs list on `nextRuns.length > 0` (L48), preserving the web React keys key={p.value} (L37) and key={i} (L51).

i18n intent preserved: react-i18next is not wired in native, so useTranslation()'s t (L10) is replaced by useNativeTranslationFallback returning the i18n key when no default is supplied (i18next returns the key for a missing translation). Every key is preserved verbatim: 'Every Minute'/'Every Hour'/'Every Day'/'Every Week'/'Every Month' (L18-22), 'Cron Parser'/'Cron Parser Desc' (L26), 'Cron Expression' (L29), 'Description' (L44), 'Next Runs' (L50).

Visual intent preserved: ToolCard icon=Timer color=green (L26) -> a green ICON_COLOR_MAP ring (bg rgba(52,211,153,0.10) + border rgba(52,211,153,0.20) + colors.success glyph) carrying a 'TM' glyph; the Input leading Timer icon (L33) -> a muted 'TM' leading glyph. div className=space-y-3 (L27) -> rowGap 12; the description box rounded bg-[var(--surface-overlay)] px-3 py-2 (L43) -> the dark --surface-overlay rgba(15,23,42,0.5); text-emerald-300 description (L45) -> #6ee7b7; Badge variant=info size=sm (L53) -> a blue-900/blue-200 (#1e3a8a/#bfdbfe) rounded-full chip; text-xs font-mono text-secondary run rows (L52,L54) -> a Menlo/monospace AppText. GlassPanel/Input/Button/Badge and div/span/p/input/button become the shared native GlassPanel + RN View/TextInput/Pressable + AppText.

formatDateTime (L7,L54) maps to the native lib/format parity of @/lib/dateFormat (the same module the sibling AlertDetailTimeline port reuses). getNextCronRuns yields Date objects, so each Date is passed as d.toISOString() at the call boundary — it round-trips to the identical instant and lib/format renders it in the same local wall-clock zone via Intl.DateTimeFormat. The web year-bearing format vs the native month/day/time format is the same standardized native date-format choice already accepted across the native parity surface.

No DOM, lucide-react, Recharts, Leaflet, browser HTML elements (div/span/p/input/button), or old web ui components are imported — only react-native primitives (Platform/Pressable/StyleSheet/TextInput/View), React hooks, the shared native GlassPanel + AppText, the native lib/format formatDateTime, and the theme tokens. An optional style + testID prop pair was added for native composability (defaults to {} and a stable 'cron-parser-tool' testID); the file has no API calls.
